note: bon is an adjective (agrees with a noun); bien is an adverb (modifies a verb).
an for a plain count (deux ans); année when the duration itself is felt (toute l'année, une bonne année).
jour for a plain count or a point in time; journée when the span of the day is felt (toute la journée).
soir for a plain point in time; soirée when the span or the event itself is felt (une bonne soirée, une soirée entre amis).
matin for a plain point in time; matinée when the span is felt (toute la matinée).
depuis names the starting point of something still going on; pendant names a bounded span, often finished.
très intensifies; trop means an excessive amount, often with a negative or limiting sense.
encore means still or again, often about something expected to end; toujours means always, or still in the sense of persisting.
savoir for facts, information and skills (savoir + infinitive, savoir que); connaître for people, places and things you are familiar with.
apporter brings a thing toward the point of reference; emporter takes a thing away from it.
amener brings a person or animal toward the point of reference; emmener takes them away from it.
emprunter is to borrow (take); prêter is to lend (give temporarily).
partir leaves with no object (partir de Paris); sortir is to go out or exit; quitter always needs a direct object (quitter la maison, quitter quelqu'un).
chez is at or to a person's home or practice (chez le médecin); à is at or to a place or institution (à l'école).
visiter is for a place; rendre visite à is for a person.
